process.detail: We confirm cooking volume, hood length, duct length, access panel count and the window that keeps your kitchen running.
Crews work the hood, plenum, duct runs and fans to bare metal, including overnight shifts when the line cannot stop.
Photographs of each surface before and after, grease thickness recorded by location, access panels resealed and painted.
Certificate, photo set and deficiency list issued within 24 hours, with the next cleaning date set to your cooking volume.

assurance.title: NFPA 96 cleaning frequency
assurance.detail: Frequency is set by cooking volume and hours of operation, from monthly on high-volume charbroiling to annually on low-volume equipment, and we document the basis for the schedule we recommend.

assurance.title: Trained, insured crews
assurance.detail: Field crews are trained on hood and duct cleaning practice, carry current insurance certificates and are bonded for commercial kitchen work.

assurance.title: Proof an inspector accepts
assurance.detail: Every visit produces cleaning certificates, a dated photo set, grease-thickness readings and a signed service report retained for five years.

assurance.title: No-surprise pricing
assurance.detail: The written scope lists hood, duct, fan and containment work line by line, so the invoice matches the quote and the schedule does not drift.

faq.q: How often does NFPA 96 require kitchen exhaust cleaning?
faq.a: Cleaning frequency follows cooking volume and hours of operation: monthly for solid-fuel and high-volume charbroiling, quarterly for moderate-volume cooking, semiannually for low-volume cooking and annually for equipment that is seldom used. We assess your line and put the basis for the frequency in writing.

faq.q: Can you clean without shutting down service?
faq.a: Yes. Most of our work runs overnight or between service periods. Cleaning windows are booked around your prep schedule and, when the line cannot stop, the crew works section by section.

faq.q: What documentation do we receive after each visit?
faq.a: A cleaning certificate, a dated photo set of the hood, plenum, duct and fan, grease-thickness readings by location, and a deficiency list with severity and recommended correction dates. Everything is issued within 24 hours of the visit.

faq.q: Do you work with multi-unit operators and franchise groups?
faq.a: Yes. Location lists, standing schedules and consolidated reporting are standard for multi-unit operators, and each site keeps its own certificate history.

faq.q: What happens after a fire marshal or insurance inspection notice?
faq.a: Send the notice and the inspection report. We schedule the corrective cleaning, document each cited item, and issue the follow-up certificate set your inspector needs to close the file.
